fieldScore.title: Field performance
fieldScore.explanation: Expected win rate against the current tournament field: each opponent's meta share × matchup win rate, the mirror counts as 50 %. Higher = better positioned against the field.

fieldScore.matchupSource: Matchup data: TrainerHill · as of {{date}} · mixed Bo1/Bo3 format, treat as approximate
fieldScore.noMatchups: No matchup data imported — the score rests on the mirror only.
fieldScore.intervalHint: Two separate questions: coverage says how much of the field has data at all; this interval says how sure we are about the number for the part that does.

methodology.rank: Rank: tournament decklists with nearly identical cards (55 of 60 or more matching) are merged into one cluster and sorted by the lower bound of the estimated win rate (a Wilson score), not the raw win rate — so a list with few games and a lucky run doesn't automatically land on top.
methodology.interval: The percentage and range (e.g. 55.2–83.0 %) are the estimated true win rate with a 95% confidence interval — the more games recorded in this cluster, the narrower the range.
methodology.record: The record sums wins and losses across every list in this cluster, not just the one example list shown.
methodology.placement: Avg. placement is the average tournament percentile across all cluster members — "top 1%" means it placed, on average, in the best 1% of the field.
methodology.fieldScore: The field score (when shown) is the same win rate, but weighted against your configured local field instead of evenly against every opponent.

methodology.rank: Rank: this archetype's decklists at this tournament with nearly identical cards (55 of 60 or more matching) are merged into one cluster and sorted by the lower bound of the estimated win rate (a Wilson score), not the raw win rate.
methodology.interval: The percentage and range are the estimated true win rate with a 95% confidence interval — the more games recorded in this cluster, the narrower the range.
methodology.record: The record sums wins and losses across every list in this cluster at this tournament, not just the one example list shown.
methodology.placement: Avg. placement is the average tournament percentile across all cluster members — "top 1%" means it placed, on average, in the best 1% of the field.
methodology.fieldScore: The field score is the same win rate, but weighted against this one tournament's actual field, not a multi-tournament window.

equilibrium.title: Game-theoretic view (experimental)
equilibrium.intro: This view shows which decks game theory says belong in the optimal mix – not how popular they currently are. It adds a second, robustness-checked perspective alongside the field score and does not replace it.
equilibrium.notAReplacement: Complements the field score, does not replace it.

robust.veryRobust: {{name}} is a poor choice in almost every scenario
robust.robust: {{name}} is a poor choice in most scenarios
robust.likelyIn: {{name}} belongs in the mix in most scenarios

composition.title: Exact composition
composition.fragile: This exact composition is unstable: small changes in the matchup data would lead to a noticeably different mix. Rely on the robust statements above rather than the precise percentages here.

coverage.thin: relies mostly on missing matchup data

equilibrium.sourceImputed: {{pct}} % of matchup cells have no data
equilibrium.methodNote: The calculation assumes a zero-sum game (win rate + opponent win rate = 100 %) and symmetrizes conflicting matchup numbers between two decks. It does not account for correlations between matchups and is only as good as the underlying tournament data.
